title: Measured comparison with 2024-2026 template-matching, pose and few-shot counting methods
question: Where does this project's NCC matcher (stable core and research pipeline) beat or lose to PoseMatch-TDCM, GeCo2 and an OpenCV matchTemplate baseline on the same inputs, scored by one independent scorer, with accuracy, time and memory kept apart?

hypotheses.H1: Group A positives: (a) ours_fullgpu_k3 strict recall >= TDCM-adapted (primary pipeline, CPU) strict recall on every case, and >= OpenCV's on every case OpenCV completed; (b) on pooled A positives the median position and angle errors of ours_fullgpu_k3's association pairs are below TDCM-adapted's; (c) pooled box recall at IoU >= 0.5 of ours_fullgpu_k3 >= GeCo2's (MPS outputs, per the user). H1 passes when (a), (b) and (c) pass.
hypotheses.H2: B2: GeCo2 (MPS) AP50 > ours_fullgpu_k3 AP50 on the FSCD-147 mirror test boxes, both by literature_score (pooled 101-point, IoU 0.5); judged only if the authenticity gate passes, otherwise held per geco2_mps_stop; if AP50 is retired: GeCo2 count MAE < ours count MAE against FSC points.
hypotheses.H3: C tiny templates under the official 36x36 weights (rewritten per the user; the paper's 12x12 result is cited, not reproduced): TDCM-adapted pooled strict recall on the tiny-template positives >= ours_fullgpu_k3's.
hypotheses.H4: On >= 4096x4096 multi-object scenes (many128_pose, many512_pose, many8k_512), same M4 Pro: ours_fullgpu_k3 per-image call time < TDCM-adapted CPU per-image call time on each scene.
hypotheses.H5: A negatives (empty_scene, constant_source, 7 wrong-template scenes): every ours arm reports 0 false positives; competitors' false positives reported, GeCo2 N/A.

Phase 1 runner smoke overlapped round 49's dev_calibrate lock at 09:50:07Z (<1 s), disclosed in both rounds.

order and stop rules: (1) literature_geco2_cuda_precheck.py must pass all four checks (torch sees the GPU with sm_120; the compiled extension is the imported module and its CUDA forward matches ms_deform_attn_core_pytorch in float64 within 1e-4; one image gives finite boxes with the compiled module; the checkpoint leaves exactly the 149 sam_mask keys missing, all identical across two init seeds, i.e. loaded from SAM2, and the same 8 unused auxiliary-head keys as on the Mac), otherwise nothing runs; (2) the B2 batch over all 1,190 test images (3-hour timeout) and the authenticity gate |AP - 46.81| <= 2 and |AP50 - 75.89| <= 2 (literature_geco2_fscd_eval.py); (3) gate pass: group A and C positive cases (16 + 72) through literature_geco2_cuda_run.py, one fresh process per case, 1 warm-up + 1 measured call, 8 threads, then summarize --geco2-accuracy geco2_cuda for H1(c), H2 and the B2 GeCo2 rows; gate miss: AP50 is retired and H2 becomes count MAE against FSC points from the same CUDA batch, and the A/C runs wait for the lead session. Every attempt is a manifest row; failures are kept and never rerun; a restart after a host failure reruns only cases without a row and records the attempt number.

Lab-PC times are descriptive, shown beside the M4 Pro times per hardware and never divided against them; every worker records the 1-minute load and nvidia-smi utilisation and memory in use (WSL shows no per-process GPU users), recorded not gated. Memory: peak RSS (literature_geco2_worker.py now reports Linux ru_maxrss KiB as bytes) and CUDA max allocated/reserved, never added. Our arms are not rerun (the acceptance replay already showed the af7c97a-equivalent block 0 identical).

Environment instead: native Windows on PTRI-PRO-4000 (Windows 10.0.26300, Intel Core Ultra 9 285K 24 cores, 63.5 GiB, RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell 24 GB sm_120, driver 596.71 kept), Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools C++ workload (MSVC v143), CUDA 12.8.1 toolkit subpackages without Display.Driver (installer md5 checked against NVIDIA's md5sum.txt), a Python 3.12 venv with torch 2.7.1+cu128 win_amd64 and the M4 Pro versions of the other packages, the official extension built with MSVC for TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0 (literature_geco2_cuda_setup.ps1). Any change to GeCo2's ops sources or setup.py needed on Windows is a protocol deviation: git status and git diff of the GeCo2 tree are saved after the build and every change is disclosed in the report. An installer that asks for a reboot stops the setup and is reported to the lead session. Long processes start through Win32_Process.Create so that they survive the SSH session. Peak memory on Windows is the process's peak working set (GetProcessMemoryInfo); Windows has no load average, so each worker row records the CPU LoadPercentage instead (load1 null). The order, stop rules and reporting of the previous three revisions are unchanged.
